text:
Sunshine has done its job this Monday. We're already in the mid 60s with clear skies, and the afternoon tops out near 68, which is well above normal for early November. A high-pressure system sliding off to our south is turning the flow southerly and pulling in the mild air. With the sun setting around 4:40, the best window for a walk or a ride is the next couple of hours, and a light layer will do.

Clouds thicken tonight, and it stays mild with a low around 52. Tuesday turns gray and cooler, with a high near 60. A few showers could pass through, mostly from about 2 to 5 in the afternoon. They'd be light, under a tenth of an inch, so a jacket is enough and you won't need to cancel anything. The models lean a little wetter than the official forecast, so I'd keep an umbrella handy.

Then it warms up again. Wednesday looks like the warmest day of the week, in the low 70s and close to record territory. Steady rain arrives Thursday, heaviest Thursday night.
